reader.requirement: At --std 85, a WRITE to a sequential file executes only when the file is open in the output or extend mode; on a file not open, open INPUT or open I-O (any WRITE form: plain, FROM, ADVANCING, END-OF-PAGE), the WRITE is unsuccessful with I-O status 48 (§1985:VII.1.3.5) and writes nothing.
reader.edition-search: grep Dialect|Edition|CobolVersion|Std in SequentialConnector.cs: none; in SequentialIoBinder.cs only ctx.Edition for diagnostic reporting and the FORMAT clause level, not on the WRITE mode test. Both WRITE entry points test 'Mode is not (Output or Extend)' -> '48' unconditionally.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f20_03 covers plain WRITE never-opened, OUTPUT, EXTEND, INPUT, I-O; not exercised there: WRITE FROM, the ADVANCING arm, a LINAGE file with END-OF-PAGE, WRITE after CLOSE and after a failed OPEN

probes.printed: NEVER-OPENED FROM 48 / OUTPUT 00 / AFTER-CLOSE 48 / INPUT ADVANCING 48 / I-O ADV PAGE 48 / EXTEND 00 / LINAGE OUTPUT 00 / LINAGE INPUT 48 / FAILED OPEN EXTEND 35 / WRITE AFTER FAILED OPEN 48; the data file holds only the AAAA and BBBB records (12 bytes, print-line framing because F is written with ADVANCING)
probes.expected: 48 for every WRITE not in output or extend mode, 00 in OUTPUT and EXTEND, nothing written by a refused WRITE

probes.printed: each refused form (plain, FROM, AFTER ADVANCING 2, BEFORE ADVANCING PAGE, END-OF-PAGE/NOT END-OF-PAGE) answered 48 and ran no END-OF-PAGE imperative
probes.expected: GR1 violated in each WRITE form -> unsuccessful, status 48

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR1  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.4g

reader.notes: The mode test sits at the top of both WRITE bodies, after only the permanent-error replay, so it binds every WRITE form; it is edition-invariant and matches 1985's status 48 for a sequential file (I-O mode is refused, as 1985 requires). Side observation: a record-sequential file once written WITH ADVANCING is framed as print lines, so reading it back with fixed 4-byte records misaligns (R1 '\nAAA'); that is GR16h's implementor-defined page representation, not this rule.
